messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Because RFP timelines tend to compress at the end, I expect the turnaround for this work to be last-minute, although I suspect the RFP itself will be released next quarter. Nadia, I’m seeking layout and design support for the resulting response (proposal), which will need to follow strict rules for file size, page numbers, and similar details. 1) Have you supported this type of proposal before? 2) If so, how do you prepare with clients for these timelines, particularly when client edits may continue until the proposal is final?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi Leona,

Strict compliance and compressed turnaround times are familiar territory for me; I regularly support RFP responses governed by page limits, file-size restrictions, formatting rules, and firm deadlines. This has been the core of my design work for the last 22+ years.

For condensed schedules, I structure the process this way:
• As soon as the RFP is released, I immediately create a compliant template and verify every technical requirement, including margins, fonts, file size, and submission details
• Your internal workplan and review schedule guide my timing, while I retain enough flexibility to accommodate rolling edits
• During the final 96–120 hours, I reserve my schedule exclusively for redline reviews, last-minute content drops, QA/QC, and final PDF optimization

Having managed this process many times, I can remain composed under pressure while ensuring that the submission is polished, compliant, and delivered by the deadline.

I’d be glad to arrange a call about your specific RFP and how my qualifications could support your team.

Best regards,
Nadia

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Thank you, Nadia—this is music to my ears! By Friday afternoon, I’ll send you some possible dates for a call.

Thanks again, and until then!

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: For next Wednesday (3/18), I’m free at any point from 9-11am. Would you be available during that window? Just a heads-up: the other team members I’m partnering with may want to join the call too. Thanks!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
If there’s any material you’d like me to review beforehand, feel free to send it over. Good morning—and that timing is perfect: 9–11am MST on Wednesday works for me, and anyone from your team is welcome to join the call.

I’ll share the meeting scheduler through Upwork.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Good morning! The time zone I intended was PT rather than MST. While I choose a time, could you also confirm whether there is a fee for our call? Thank you!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
There’s no fee for the call, and the time is perfect.

Talk to you soon.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Wonderful, many thanks!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I really enjoyed learning more about your upcoming proposal during our conversation today, so thank you for your time. It seems we’d work well together, and I’m looking forward to the next step.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Thank you, Nadia—the same to you! After reviewing the current proposal, I found that the full document totals 126 pages, including all letters, forms, and other materials. Of those 126 pages, 74 pages have a graphic touch. Could you provide an approximate budget range for supporting the project? Please include one budget with 3 simple infographics and 2 simple maps, plus a separate budget without those items. Thank you!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
That information really helps—perfect!

Here are the two budget options you requested:
\- Without the optional graphics: $6,200–$7,100
\- With 3 simple infographics and 2 simple maps: $6,900–$7,900

For custom proposal design of this kind, my usual estimate is 2.5 to 3 hours per page across the 74 design-focused pages. This covers layout and graphic treatment, all meetings and revisions, on-demand support during the final 72 hours before submission, delivery of the completed full document, and general proposal support throughout the process.

We can proceed either hourly or on a fixed-fee basis, whichever works best for you. Does this fall within the range you had in mind? I’m happy to adjust the estimate based on your feedback.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Before I respond, I’ll discuss it with the rest of the team. Thanks, Nadia—I’ll hopefully get back to you by the middle of next week.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Have a wonderful week as well!

messages.text:
Following up on your note from last week, Leona: has the team had an opportunity to discuss it, and are there any questions on your end?

If it would be useful, I’m happy to jump on a quick call.

Thank you,
Nadia

The scope covers packaging all content into one doc., along with layout, the org. chart, the budget sheet, and formatting. Although the response is due 9/16, I plan to submit it on 9/15. Would you be interested in helping me with this task? If so, could you provide the total cost? I’ll also send the RFQ shortly for reference. Thanks!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
With the additional detail, I now have a much clearer understanding of the scope. For the anticipated page count and RFQ, I would charge $5,200 for the project.

The fee covers:
- Creative direction and proposal design
- Layout and graphic treatment across the full document
- Creation of a cohesive visual theme aligned with the RFQ and the client
- Integration of graphics, photos, tables, and any other necessary visual elements
- Meetings, revisions, and ongoing support, including on-demand assistance leading up to submission
- Final production and delivery of the complete proposal package

If that arrangement works for you, the next steps would be for me to send a proposed contract through Upwork and schedule a brief kickoff call so we can align on the timeline, proposal strategy, and design direction.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Unfortunately, the earlier proposal is beyond my budget and includes more scope than I need. Could the simpler version instead focus on a single formatting/layout pass over the final draft, using Civic Canopy's existing brand colors and fonts, followed by one round of revisions and delivery as a print-ready PDF?

More specifically, what I need is 1) layout and graphic treatment for the complete document and 2) application of the tables, photos, org chart, and graphics to the final draft.

Because the RFQ is usually the first step, I suspect there is also a chance that an RFP will follow later. What would this reduced version cost?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
For $3,100, I can adapt the scope to a single formatting/layout pass on the final draft, using Civic Canopy's existing colors and fonts and allowing for one round of revisions.

That scope would cover:
- Graphic treatment and layout of the entire document
- Placement of tables, photos, the org chart, and other graphics into the final draft
- One round of revisions
- Delivery of both a print-ready PDF and an editable Canva design link

To protect the schedule and budget, I would prefer to receive all finalized materials together, including the text, tables, photos, org chart, and any other supporting content. I will need six business days to prepare the first draft, followed by five days for revisions. Because the layout will be built in Canva, you or your team can make any remaining content changes after the included revision rounds.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
The estimate you sent, $3100.00, works for me. Thank you.

A few follow-up items:

1) Would a 72-hour turnaround for the draft after I provide the final narrative, followed by a 72-hour turnaround on your end for final revisions, be workable? My subcontractors will not send their content until EOD next Friday, so your working window will be compressed.

2) I have shifted the branding from the client to the bidder—me—so please design it around my company's identity, Blue Mesa Strategies. I can provide the logo and colors.

3) This will be the first proposal I submit as a prime (I launched my company less than a year ago, and I’m solo), so I want it to serve as a reusable template and not have to rebuild future proposals from scratch. Please make the sections swappable and modular: a) a flexible narrative structure (for example, 12 sections vs. 18 sections), b) a modular table style that resizes for different budget structures, and c) a “prepared for ___ [client name]” credit line rather than client branding.

4) Canva: Will I still own the files if I do not have a paid subscription? Will source files exist in another format, or will everything be entirely in Canva?

Thank you!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Congratulations on the launch of Blue Mesa Strategies! It’s exciting to be part of your first proposal as a prime.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
1) Monday the 14th is when I would handle revisions; before that, I would prepare the first draft on Wednesday the 9th and Thursday the 10th. That timing works on my end.

2) Please send the logo, colors, and any other reference content I should use. I’m happy to build the design around Blue Mesa Strategies' identity rather than Civic Canopy's.

3) Would you prefer that I quote the modular template as an add-on now, or should we keep this proposal simple and revisit the template later as a separate project? Although the system you described would be valuable over the long term, it falls outside the quoted scope for a one-proposal layout. Accommodating future proposals with different section counts and budget structures requires additional design and testing, so creating that system should be priced separately to keep the arrangement fair to both of us. I would be glad to build it.

4) After the file is built, you will receive full editing access and ownership, allowing you to reuse and adapt it independently for future proposals by changing client information, content, and project details. I will also use only free Canva assets, ensuring that no Pro-only elements are tied to the file.

In the meantime, if you can send over your branding documents, I can prepare the cover page, table of contents, and general layout in anticipation of the content.

Quick update, Leona—good morning. The design is about halfway complete, and I’ll incorporate the updated tables and biographies you shared.

Because the document is about three times the length anticipated in the initial scope, I’m keeping the proposal clean, organized, and easy to navigate rather than adding excessive visual complexity. The final design will therefore be more streamlined, using consistent layouts and fewer custom treatments for individual sections so that the content and overall flow remain central.

I’ll keep working through the pages that remain and update you as the design progresses.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Thanks—this approach works for me.

I hadn’t anticipated the document becoming this long, so I’m hoping we can tighten the spacing between paragraphs and sections to bring it closer to the original page limit. When I reach the review, I’d also like to condense the letter \(first page\) to one page.

If anything else feels awkward, I can try cutting the content further during my review if doing so would help. I appreciate you collaborating with me and continuing to share progress updates.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Leona,

Two points need your guidance as you review the attached first draft of the proposal:

\- **Section 11: Prioritization:** Because this section did not appear in the updated tables document, I’m still unsure whether it belongs in the proposal.

\- **In-text bolding:** The intended bold formatting was also unclear. Some passages in the Google Doc were highlighted while others appeared in red, and after moving into layout, I couldn’t determine which treatments were intentional and which were editorial markup.

The editable Canva version is available here: <https://design.blue-mesa.example/civic-canopy-brief-4821>

For context on the visual approach, the document grew roughly threefold while the timeline remained tight, so I built a consistent design system instead of creating numerous unique layouts. That consistency should also make revisions easier to manage. To support the overall theme without distracting from the content, I used organic-shaped image frames along with a few understated graphic elements.

Separately, all hyperlinks were tested and appeared to work, though I’d appreciate having a second reviewer click through each one as well.

Given the tight turnaround, I’ll make another pass tomorrow with fresh eyes to catch anything I missed, but I wanted to get this to you today.

I look forward to your feedback. Hopefully the proposal is in a good place, and once you’ve reviewed it, I can fine-tune anything you want adjusted.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Thank you—wonderful work and a very quick turnaround! I’ll be tied up in meetings for a while, but this afternoon I’ll do one last full read. Afterward, I’ll let you know whether I need any additional support. 👍

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: While reviewing between meetings, I noticed one item, Nadia, and will post any further issues here as I find them. 1) The crop on page 23 has lost the intended view of the tree. Could you zoom out slightly so a little more of the tree becomes visible again? Thanks.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: My review is still underway, and I’m aiming to finish by 3:15pm. I’ve made several small wording adjustments that did not affect the formatting. A few formatting items from yesterday are still outstanding, though they’re very minor, like the photo mentioned above. I wanted to flag them for you; each one is recorded in the Comments on the current version. Once I’m completely finished, I’ll let you know. Thanks!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Sounds good, Leona. The last 8 comments are now resolved, and I’ve adjusted the image as requested. After 3:15pm, I’ll check again to determine whether anything else needs attention.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: thanks

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: My review is complete. Once you’ve resolved anything still outstanding from yesterday, please let me know when this version has been finalized and exported as an emailable PDF. Thank you!

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: PS The plan is still to email the document to CC today. Thanks.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Because no comments remained open, I completed the export using the digital distribution settings provided by Canva. The resulting file is well below the standard 25mb size limit.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Fantastic! Before sending the document, I’ll test the hyperlinks in this version. Once that review is complete, I’ll send it and follow up afterward.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Hopefully, everything worked properly!

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Everything worked, and CC confirmed receipt after I emailed the submission! WAHOOO! I’m incredibly grateful for your partnership throughout this process. The work is beautiful, and you were exceptionally professional—staying on schedule and even moving tasks earlier than expected.

I’m excited to tell RCP how great it was to work with you on this product. I’ll keep you in mind for future proposals and will gladly refer you to colleagues as well. I also plan to leave a review on Upwork. MIL GRACIAS DE NUEVO!!! :)

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I just noticed that I hadn’t released the payment earlier. It appears to have gone through now, though I’m not yet certain. Sorry for the delay, and thanks again!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
It was a pleasure working with you too—thank you so much! Your clear communication and organization made the entire process run very smoothly from my side.

I’m delighted that the submission was completed successfully, and I look forward to resuming the RCP work next spring.

Thank you as well for releasing the payment and leaving an Upwork review; as you know, that support truly makes a difference.

Have a wonderful weekend. I’m looking forward to collaborating again!
